Filters, brake & clutch cover  |  FY2024 - FY2026  |
What actually counts in each measure
GPS shows the size of the prize. PMS shows exactly where it's slipping away.
Counts every genuine Isuzu part number sold into a market — engines, body, electrical, everything — against everything that market could realistically buy genuine.

Out of every euro a workshop could spend genuine,
how much do we actually capture?
Same logic as PMS: actual, potential — a broad, market-wide health check.
Looks only at competitive, interval-driven items — oil and air filters, brake pads, clutch kits, lubricants — things every vehicle needs on a fixed schedule.

Out of the parts a workshop is replacing anyway,
on schedule, how many are ours?
A focused diagnostic — it tells us which specific categories are leaking to non-genuine alternatives.
From parc size to captured sales and gap visibility
GPS — same actual / potential / coverage logic, full parts basket
PMS — focused leakage model for interval-driven items

GPS = Actual genuine sales ÷ Potential parts demand
PMS Coverage = Actual PMS sales ÷ Potential PMS demand
Scope is refined per market: filters, brake, clutch, lubricants and other competitive maintenance items with service-interval logic.
PMS modeling assumptions — what's confirmed vs. assumed

—  None of the wear-part factors (brake, clutch) are confirmed for Israel specifically - the underlying actual sales figures are solid; the demand-model denominators are the assumption layer on top.
—  The clutch-equipped parc share and the 50,000 km/yr mileage figure both originate from another market's data and convention, not from a UTI or Israel-specific source - flagged, not fixed, in this deck.
—  Capture % should be read as directional until confirmed service-interval ratios exist for UTI specifically.
Revenue grew through FY2025, eased back in FY2026

—  Total PMS revenue rose to EUR 426K in FY2025 (+24% vs FY2024), then eased back to EUR 365K in FY2026 (-14% vs FY2025, still +6% vs FY2024).
—  Cover against modeled demand (8 active categories, 100% of UTI's PMS revenue) sits at 34% (FY2024) -> 42% (FY2025) -> 36% (FY2026) — most of the addressable basket is still going elsewhere.
—  The FY2026 pullback is concentrated in two categories — oil filter and clutch kit — not a basket-wide slowdown. Fuel and air filter kept growing through the same period (see following slides).
Filters are the strongest performer — air filter leads

—  Air filter is the strongest trend: 36% -> 48% -> 58% cover, climbing every year — the one category moving consistently the right way.
—  Fuel filter has also grown fast: 49% -> 72% -> 75%.
—  Oil filter is the exception — it grew to 55% in FY2025, then dropped back to 31% in FY2026 as volume fell from 6,976 to 4,046 units. Worth asking UTI directly why oil filter alone reversed while fuel and air kept climbing.
—  Model: IML v7 (Isuzu Japan) schedule — 40,000 km service interval, 1.25 services/year, 100% addressable. All figures capped at (and currently below) 100%.
Brake & clutch: the real whitespace in the basket

—  Both categories run well below filters — the clearest remaining whitespace in the UTI PMS basket.
—  Brake pad is steady in the high-20s to low-30s% across all three years (30% -> 33% -> 27%), no clear direction.
—  Clutch kit fell sharply in FY2026 — 37% down to 18%, a 49% drop in units (869 -> 442 kits) — the single biggest swing anywhere in the basket. Worth raising directly with UTI.
—  Clutch scored as complete jobs (kit = full disc+plate+bearing job), not against a narrow per-part slice — the correct read, but the 100,000 km interval and the clutch-equipped parc share are still assumptions carried over from another market, not UTI-measured.
Clutch capture roughly halved - worth asking why

—  Blending all clutch sub-categories together, capture went 35.4% to 38.7% to 20.3% across the three fiscal years shown.
—  The FY2025 to FY2026 drop (38.7% to 20.3%) is a real trend, not a modeling artifact - it survives the denominator fix.
—  Open question for the meeting: what changed for UTI's clutch business between FY2025 and FY2026 - competitor entry, a stocking gap, or a fleet-age shift?
Air filter overtakes clutch kit as the top revenue line

—  Air filter has overtaken clutch kit as the single largest PMS revenue line — EUR 141K in FY2026 vs clutch kit's EUR 52K, a reversal from FY2024/25 when they were roughly level.
—  Clutch kit's revenue fall (EUR 107K -> 52K, -51%) is proportionally worse than its cover-% fall (37% -> 18%) suggests on its own — this is the biggest single EUR swing in the whole basket.
—  Oil filter revenue fell EUR 18K (59K -> 41K) alongside its cover drop — consistent with a real volume pullback, not just a modeling artifact.
—  Fuel filter and brake pad are comparatively stable contributors (EUR 80-85K and EUR 42-50K respectively across the three years).
Clutch kit's gap is growing, not shrinking

—  Clutch kit carries the single largest gap in the basket every year — and it's growing, not shrinking (EUR 213K -> 185K -> 235K) — the opposite direction from what the revenue trend alone would suggest.
—  Brake pad's gap has also widened in FY2026 (EUR 99K -> 116K) as volume eased off.
—  Air filter's gap is shrinking fast (EUR 157K -> 102K) — proof the growth there is closing real whitespace, not just growing off a low base.
—  These are ceiling figures (cost of reaching 100% modeled demand, not a forecast) — useful for prioritising where to focus, not as a sales target.
